issues.legal_issue: A revisional court may not interfere with lower courts’ decision merely because of an error of law when those courts had jurisdiction to decide the dispute and committed no procedural error.
material_facts: The Rent Controller, the appellate authority, and the District Court found that the building had been leased for both trade and residence.
The landlord did not establish that any part of the building was being used for a purpose different from the purpose for which it was leased.
The High Court interfered with the lower courts’ decision in revision, although they had jurisdiction to decide the dispute and had committed no procedural error.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not entitled to interfere in revision, and the appeal was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an error of law, however gross, does not by itself permit revisional interference where the lower courts had jurisdiction to decide the dispute and committed no procedural error. The Court applied the principles in Keshardeo Chamria v. Radha Kissen Chamria and Others and Pandurang Dhoni Chougule v. Maruti Hari Jadhav.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_revisional_interference and lower_courts_had_authority_to_decide and no_procedural_error_occurred and lower_courts_concurred_on_lease_purpose and different_use_not_shown

predicates.appeal_challenges_revisional_interferenc: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a revisional court’s interference with a lower-court decision.
predicates.lower_courts_had_authority_to_decide: The lower courts had authority to decide the dispute before them.
predicates.no_procedural_error_occurred: The lower courts committed no procedural error in deciding the dispute.
predicates.lower_courts_concurred_on_lease_purpose: The lower courts agreed on the purpose for which the property had been leased.
predicates.different_use_not_shown: The party alleging a use different from the leased purpose did not establish that such a different use occurred.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges revisional interference and the lower courts had authority to decide, committed no procedural error, agreed on the lease purpose, and no different use was shown, revisional interference is unjustified.
